results.strategy_description:
LGT Risk Premia SF is a largely market-neutral and dynamic long/short quantitative macro strategy with a live track record since April 2016. The fund has been designed to harness systematic premia beyond market beta, thus providing a truly uncorrelated alpha stream of returns. More specifically, the fund targets consistent long-term capital appreciation with an expected volatility of below 10% and an equity market beta of <0.3 measured over a rolling 3-5 year period. 

The investment process combines a machine-learning based, top-down portfolio construction framework with a diversified set of 30 systematic trading strategies aimed at generating performance from alternative risk premiums and lead-lag effects extracted bottom-up within and across over 200 liquid markets globally in all major asset classes, i.e., equity indices, single stocks, government bonds, money markets, interest rate swaps, currencies, commodities, and volatility.

results.strategy_description:
LGT Dynamic Protection is a quantitative crisis alpha strategy aiming to deliver the return profile of an equity put option without paying costly premiums for tail risk protection. More specifically, the strategy seeks to deliver strong capital gains during phases of elevated equity market stress while limiting the costs of carry in normal periods, thus providing a highly asymmetric return profile which makes the strategy a particularly valuable diversifier in a balanced portfolio context  - especially in comparison to solely relying on bonds for cushioning equity risks or trying to time markets with option-based crisis risk offset approaches. 

The strategy is well-diversified across different markets and asset classes, fully systematic and entirely futures-based in its implementation. It combines a top-down risk budgeting framework linked to equity market volatility with an equally weighted basket of eight fundamentally anchored and dynamically sized hedging strategies that exploit their risk budgets bottom-up. Each sub-strategy has its own diversified set of proprietary signals and trades independent from the others with trading speeds ranging from mid- to short term up to intraday and overnight. At portfolio level, this results in a high degree of versatility and robustness and allows the LGT Dynamic Protection strategy to cope with a wide range of possible future crisis scenarios.

results.strategy_description: At Quantique – Machine, Math & Mind, the investment decision, selection, and allocation process combines the discipline of data-driven quantitative models with the rigorous oversight of seasoned financial professionals. Our objective is to deliver beta-neutral, alpha-generating strategies that maximize the Sharpe ratio. The process begins with the acquisition and preparation of large volumes of market data through Extract, Transform, and Load procedures, ensuring that information is thoroughly cleaned and structured for use in our models. Once prepared, this data serves as the foundation for robust signal extraction. Using advanced statistical and machine-learning techniques, our proprietary models generate signals that identify investment opportunities by capturing inefficiencies across liquid emerging and developed markets. These signals are then assessed under explicit risk parameters and portfolio constraints, with the resulting insights feeding directly into portfolio optimization, where models are designed to achieve the highest possible risk-adjusted returns. Although Quantique operates under one unified investment framework, multiple strategies are applied within each stage to enhance diversification and resilience. This multi-strategy design, combined with systematic analysis and disciplined human supervision, enables Quantique to consistently generate alpha and deliver superior Sharpe ratios across market cycles. At the same time, all strategies are constructed to remain beta-neutral and robust against directional risks. To ensure reliability and consistency, every model undergoes rigorous training, in-sample validation, and out-of-sample testing before any allocation decisions are implemented.

results.strategy_description:
The Selwood ESG Credit UCITS Fund is managed by Selwood Asset Management (France) SAS, a Paris-based team with experience in the structured credit markets and Fixed Income Investments. The goal of this strategy is to generate Investment Grade carry using an independent and passive ESG approach, all in a liquid format. The strategy’s unencumbered cash (> 80%% of the NAV) will be invested in EUR duration-hedged Green Government Bonds with a focus on core European countries. These Green Government Bonds are long-term investments that contribute to the following indicative goals: climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, and pollution prevention.
The investment team will generate returns by seeking a long exposure to iTraxx MSCI ESG Screened Index and actively managing the fund’s net exposure and Mark to Market by seeking a short exposure to iTraxx Main Europe Index. Investment decisions are made at the discretion of Selwood’s investment team and are supported by in-house indicators such as options replicating portfolios, momentum indicators, and more complex tools such as IA based tools to optimise the way we rebalance risk.
The investment strategy involves certain risks. Please refer to full details and risk factors in the Fund’s supplement. No performance guarantees.

results.management_company_description:
Led by its Founder and Portfolio Manager, Christopher DeLong, Birnam Oak Advisors, LP ("Birnam Oak" or the "Firm") is a concentrated, liquid, alpha seeking investment manager targeting the generation of superior risk adjusted returns.   The Firm looks for opportunities to capitalize upon the inefficiencies created by large pools of passive capital, the mechanistic use of "factors", and other capital flows insensitive to price discovery in the various global asset markets by investing in concentrated "information intensive" positions in merger arbitrage, capital structure arbitrage, legal/regulatory risks, volatility expressions, and highly liquid capture of duration and credit spread. Birnam Oak will also attempt to create a limited degree of downside protection by searching for, and employing, when possible, positions that it believes will create "long volatility" cheaper than can be purchased by "plain vanilla" options in the open market.

Firm AUM includes assets under management of both the Birnam Oak funds and managed accounts.  Managed account assets are presented on the basis of agreed notional account size as the account asset size does not vary with performance.  Fund assets under management are presented as of month end prior to redemptions, subscriptions and transfers.
results.strategy_description:
Birnam Oak has broad and flexible investment authority and intends to continually adjust the composition of the portfolio, which includes North American and non-North American long and short investments in equities, derivatives, debt instruments, and other securities or financial instruments, including those of investment companies. Birnam Oak constructs its alpha seeking portfolio through "bottom up" research and relies on numerous sources of publicly available information for its investment decisions.  The Firm believes it has assembled a distinguished Advisory Council of experts and regularly consults with other third-party advisors, including but not limited to, legal experts in fields such as antitrust, bankruptcy and securities law, as well as those with expertise in specific geographic (e.g., Germany, Spain, Italy) and microeconomic areas (e.g., energy, technology and utilities).
 
Birnam Oak will manage two investment sleeves on a pro rata, pari passu basis: (i) an "alpha only” sleeve, which will include the Firm’s core "alpha" portfolio investments, and (ii) an "alpha + equity risk premium” sleeve, which combines the "alpha" portfolio with a leveraged, concentrated long equity portfolio of positions generally designed to capture equity risk premium and correlate with the world equity markets.  When deemed appropriate, Birnam Oak seeks tax efficiency when managing the equity risk premium component of the alpha + equity risk premium sleeve for onshore investors only.  Mr. DeLong has been managing the combined "alpha + equity risk premium" portfolio since May 2021 and Birnam Oak will assume management of that portfolio when the Firm launches in January 2024.

The business was founded by two senior quants from BlueCrest and they were joined by a head of business development from Pictet. The team launched the flagship strategy, Diversified Alpha, in February 2016. The firm is built upon the premise of applying scientific methods to identify a wide range of opportunities within liquid financial markets. Research is at the core of the business and the team is continually striving to improve by exploring new quantitative methods, learning from the markets and enhancing processes. The aim is that with this approach the company can successfully navigate different market environments and the variety of challenges they present.

In 2022, two experienced portfolio managers joined to launch a new venture called Solken Convertible Arbitrage. This is a distinct product within DCM Systematic and combines quantitative techniques with discretionary analysis to explore opportunities in the convertible bond markets.
results.strategy_description:
Diversified Alpha uses a multi-strategy, non-trend systematic approach to trade liquid futures markets. It aims to deliver uncorrelated, absolute returns through all market environments, applying scientific methods to identify a range of alpha, diversified by asset classes and time-frames. 

Diversified Alpha runs over 30 uncorrelated strategies with a commodity focus. These strategies operate independently of one another and are each designed to capture a specific opportunity. Each has its risk system with controls and constraints that are relevant to the markets being traded and often include forward-looking scenarios. In general, they complement one another and have time horizons ranging from short- (5-10 days) to medium-term (2-8 weeks).

Risk management and portfolio construction combine longer-term strategic targets for the portfolio volatility, asset class allocations, and strategy weights with a daily optimization process designed to enable strategies to deliver their target volatility within their risk constraints. This process aims to ensure a high level of diversification by trading approach, time frame, and markets.

Research is viewed as a continuous process focused on enhancing and improving Diversified Alpha, either through discovering new sources of alpha, creating differentiated trading strategies, or updating existing processes.

results.management_company_description: Sagefield Capital, a Dallas-based hedge fund manager founded in 2019 by former Citadel Portfolio Manager Mark Schlueter and former Highland Capital Portfolio Manager Jonathan Lamensdorf, manages commingled funds and separately managed account assets. The equity-focused, market neutral multi-strategy fund includes equity relative value and event driven. The equity relative value strategy, which focuses on low-net and sector-specific investments covering Natural Resources, Utilities, Industrials, and Energy Transition, also has a standalone fund. Merger arbitrage strategies within the multi-strategy fund provide added diversification through additional uncorrelated return streams. Overall, the Firm aims to potentially deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns to investors by employing a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative research process, led by principals with extensive experience at leading investment firms.
results.strategy_description:
The Firm believes that by combining uncorrelated, market-neutral strategies into a multi-strategy fund, the Fund should be able to achieve its return objective with lower levels of volatility than could be achieved in a single strategy fund. The Investment Manager believes the overall risk of the Fund may be materially reduced due to the well-understood portfolio diversification effects received from combining such strategies together. The Firm also believes constructing a portfolio of market-neutral strategies may create a multi-strategy fund with performance that is both uncorrelated to traditional assets and absolute return driven. 

The Fund is an equity-focused, market-neutral fund employing six strategies at inception that the Investment Manager believes have little to no correlation with one another: (i) Natural Resources, (ii) Utilities, (iii) Industrials, (iv) Energy Transition, (v) Merger Arbitrage, and (vi) Special Situations. The Firm allocates capital across the Fund’s strategies by analyzing the risk and return characteristics of each individual strategy, the resulting risk/reward of the combined portfolio, as well as how the current or future market environment might affect each strategy and the Fund. The correlations of each strategy to one another and to the overall Fund are a major component of this analysis. The Firm may add additional strategies to the Fund’s portfolio over time.

We also use global indices — such as EM, S&P, Russell, or Nasdaq — to hedge specific risk factors from the portfolio.

Lastly, we may implement pair trades — such as Vale vs. Rio Tinto or Petrobras vs. international oil companies (IOCs), or even commodities indices like Brent — as additional tools to isolate macro and sector-specific risks.

results.strategy_description:
Oxbow invests long and short across Asian equity markets, as well as in non-Asian companies with significant Asia-related business drivers. The strategy has a core focus on India, Japan, Greater China, and South Korea, and employs a fundamental, concentrated and liquid approach. Key tenets of the firm's investment strategy are a collaborative and flexible research process that uses bottom-up fundamental analysis focused on assessing intrinsic value driven by earnings power and the path to value, and utilizing top-down thematic and sector analysis to develop differentiated long-term views on companies. 

Oxbow takes concentrated positions and uses clear trade construction to monetize high conviction opportunities. In addition, Oxbow strives to be patient and disciplined in position implementation and portfolio construction in order to take advantage when risk-reward dynamics move in its favor. 

Oxbow's risk management philosophy is based on the belief that the first line of defense is high conviction risk-reward assessment based on fundamentals. results.strategy_description:
Since our inception in 1995, Third Point has been an active investor in corporate credit for much of the firm’s history. The Firm’s approach to corporate credit is catalyst-driven total return expectations based on a probabilistic assessment of upside/downside rather than yield to maturity.  Third Point employs its opportunistic investment style across the entire risk spectrum, looking for attractive idiosyncratic situations in Investment Grade, High Yield, Leveraged Loans and liquid Distressed. The Firm meaningfully increased credit exposure during the Telecom distressed cycle (2001-2003), the post-GFC distressed cycle (2008-2010), the Energy sector dislocation (2015-2016) and again at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. In the wake of the GFC, Ian Wallace joined the Firm to manage the corporate credit portfolio and Stephen Schatzman joined in 2014 as the Firm began to build out our credit investment team.

In September 2024, Third Point LLC launched a dedicated credit fund, Third Point Corporate Credit Opportunities (the “Fund”), to capitalize on the Firm’s track record of investing in dislocated corporate credit securities. We believe the current market backdrop is one of the most attractive for corporate credit since the GFC, with elevated interest rates, volatility, and sector dispersion creating attractive total return opportunities in liquid credit. 

The Fund seeks to generate attractive, risk-adjusted returns across long and short investments in performing (stressed) & non-performing (distressed) credit via a liquid, open-ended structure, targeting 60-90% average net exposure. Investors have an option to elect target distributions of 3 to 5% annualized.

results.strategy_description:
The World Carbon Fund (the “Fund”) employs investment strategies across multiple regulated carbon markets. The Fund has the dual objectives to generate absolute returns with a low correlation to traditional asset classes and to have a direct impact on climate change.

The Fund deploys capital across two complementary strategies within a clearly defined risk framework: Core Strategy and Alpha Strategies. The Core Strategy seeks to generate returns from directional tactical allocations across multiple carbon markets to capture the long-term risk premium in each carbon market combined with tactical alpha. The Alpha Strategies seek to generate returns by implementing a range of short-term alpha trading strategies, which are categorised as arbitrage, short-term directional, relative value and carry. Alpha Strategies are developed with the aim to extract positive returns irrelevant of market direction by identifying inefficiencies and idiosyncratic trading opportunities. 

The World Carbon Fund has Article 9 classification under the EU Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (“SFDR”) and EU Taxonomy. It seeks, through its investment activities, to contribute directly to the reduction in global CO2 emissions. In addition, the investment advisor contributes a fixed percentage of performance fees to purchasing and cancelling carbon allowances. 

The Fund achieved its 3-year track record on 24 February 2023 and has generated a total return of 88.6% (23.6% annualised return)* from inception to 31 January 2023. Assets under management now exceed $150m.

results.esg_approach_description:
PAAMCO Prisma is committed to incorporating environmental, social, and governance (“ESG”) factors into our decision-making processes.

We have adopted ESG principles to help guide our business; they represent the values of our organization and are factors we consider when evaluating potential corporate partners and conducting business.
• Trust and Transparency: Nurture a culture where honesty, integrity and fairness are the foundation of everything we do. Have clear accountability through oversight, proper governance, and strong alignment of interest.
• Foster Diversity & Inclusion: Promote a cohesive and diverse workplace, where a breadth of experiences and backgrounds are valued as instrumental to creating optimal outcomes for all stakeholders.
• Advocate for Planet Earth: Challenge ourselves to be more cognizant of our environmental responsibility and strive to improve our environmental footprint through employee and partner education.
• Community Commitment: Engage in local communities through active participation, service, and philanthropic efforts to enrich the lives of underserved members of such communities, employees, and their families.
• Employee Wellbeing: Provide competitive pay, healthcare, training and educational opportunities, as well as other family and wellness programs.

Due Diligence – As part of our due diligence process, we engage with third-party portfolio managers (“Portfolio Managers”) to understand how they incorporate ESG factors into their investment and business management processes.
At its foundation, our assessment, which leverages themes identified by the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board, considers if a Portfolio Manager has adopted a voluntary ESG framework or established an ESG policy. Our research also includes working to understand if a Portfolio Manager identifies and considers ESG risks as part of its investment due diligence and what data sources help to inform this process. Risk professionals also leverage a third-party ESG rating resource to provide ESG snapshot scores for a Portfolio Manager’s relevant exposures; this provides another data point in understanding ESG implications for prospective Portfolio Managers.
From a business management perspective, our research helps us understand the diversity and inclusion practices of a Portfolio Manager, what types of environmental initiatives they have established for their business, and if their governance framework incorporates industry best practices.
The results of this work are included in both the investment memo and operational due diligence risk report presented to the Firm’s Investment Committee (“IC”), which is ultimately responsible for determining whether a Portfolio Manager is eligible for investment.
ESG is just one of many factors considered in an allocation decision. Our expectation is that Portfolio Managers will be at different stages of ESG integration, and as such PAAMCO Prisma will have additional ESG-specific discussions and engagement with these Portfolio Managers. PAAMCO Prisma reserves the right to reject, or withdraw from, as applicable, a Portfolio Manager whose investment program, on balance, is determined to be incompatible with the Firm’s ESG principles.
Monitoring – For Portfolio Managers approved by the IC, ESG questions will be included in an annual ESG-focused due diligence questionnaire and covered within our ongoing monitoring reviews of Portfolio Managers. Depending on a Portfolio Manager’s investment strategy, ESG may also be a more regular topic for portfolio update meetings.

Oversight & Accountability
The ESG Taskforce (the “Taskforce”), comprised of PAAMCO Prisma’s CEO and leaders from legal, compliance, portfolio management, operations, and investor services, is responsible for the ESG policy, which is ultimately reviewed and approved by the firm’s Executive Committee (“EC”).
The Taskforce, which provides periodic reporting to the EC, also:
• Coordinates ESG training and resources for employees;
• Oversees the implementation of ESG activities that support the Firm’s ESG principles;
• Regularly reviews such activities for potential enhancements;
• Works closely with the Operations and Investment teams to establish ESG reporting requested by investors; and
• Encourages collaboration with third-party organizations to improve engagement on ESG principles.

results.name: Perryridge Capital
results.management_company_description:
Perryridge Capital is is a global, bottom-up fundamental long-short fund focused on investments predominantly within the healthcare, industrials, business services and adjacent technology sectors that launched July 15, 2024.  

Perryridge’s Founder and Chief Investment Officer is Arthur Wit.  Arthur was most recently a Partner and Managing Director at Lone Pine Capital for over 10 years, and the senior investment professional responsible for healthcare and industrial investments. While at Lone Pine, Arthur pursued a substantively similar strategy and investment approach from 2013 to 2023 to that which will be deployed at Perryridge. Lone Pine Capital backed the launch of Perryridge Capital via an investment in the Perryridge Capital management company.

Perryridge seeks to be relatively concentrated with a focus on long-term value creation – compounding capital at a rate that exceeds the broader equity market with less volatility over the long term – and event-driven short selling. The investment strategy is based on a repeatable process of first-principles analysis and deep, immersive research. It seeks to preserve capital and limit volatility through disciplined underwriting, active portfolio management, and by deploying capital across diverse and uncorrelated sectors. Investments center around companies with monopolistic structure in complex and/or niche markets where there is durable growth and long-term pricing power. The Fund’s opportunity set includes companies in developed markets across the market cap spectrum with a significant portion of exposure in market capitalizations between $1B and $10B as well as in less discovered and/or under-covered companies predominantly in the U.S and Europe. 

Perryridge will deploy a concentrated portfolio of 10-20 long positions and 15-30 short positions.  Expected exposure is ~100% long by 50-60% short, although net exposure may vary from 20-70% according to the opportunity set available.  Average position sizing will be 6% for longs, with the highest conviction positions at 10-12%.  Average short position size will be 1.5% with the highest conviction shorts at 2-3%.

The firm's investment objective is to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns by applying deep expertise across the firm's core sectors, including healthcare, industrials, business services and adjacent technology companies. 
The investment strategy for the fund is based on what we believe to be a repeatable process of first-principles analysis and deep, immersive research. Perryridge will make concentrated investments in areas of elevated market inefficiency, with a focus on long-term value creation. The strategy seeks to preserve capital and limit volatility via disciplined underwriting, active portfolio management, and by deploying capital across diverse and uncorrelated sectors.
The fund’s opportunity set includes companies in developed markets across the market cap spectrum and emphasizes event-driven short selling. Perryridge will focus on areas of elevated technical and business model complexity, firms that span sector boundaries, and areas of rapid change. The portfolio will include meaningful exposure to all target sectors given the large target universe and advantages of constructing a portfolio of varied and unrelated securities.

At Tempest Peak Management, we believe sophisticated investors deserve access to differentiated opportunities backed by rigorous fundamental analysis and disciplined execution. Through our multistrategy investment platform, we deliver customized solutions across global public equities and US alternative assets, serving as a trusted partner to family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals, and select institutional clients who value long-term thinking and aligned interests. 

Our Houston-based platform leverages global networks cultivated over three decades to source and execute investments across distinct strategies. We empower family offices and ultra-high-net-worth investors with solutions that preserve generational wealth through expertise, seamless cross-border capabilities, and privileged access to exclusive opportunities.
results.strategy_description:
Tempest Peak Global Opportunities is an equity hedge fund pursuing absolute returns through disciplined value investing across global public markets. Founded in 2020 by seasoned investment professionals Vivek Rao (CIO) and David Chao (CEO), the fund targets undervalued securities worldwide using fundamental analysis and a patient capital approach.

Core Investment Philosophy: The fund identifies companies trading at significant discounts to intrinsic value with measurable catalysts for price appreciation. Unlike US-focused value strategies, the fund's global mandate provides access to a substantially larger opportunity set spanning developed and emerging markets across Asia-Pacific, Europe, Latin America, and North America.

Strategy Implementation: Portfolio construction emphasizes high-conviction positions (typically 15-25 holdings) with position sizes ranging 4-8% of net assets. The fund maintains 85-100% net long exposure with selective use of leverage not exceeding 130% gross. Investment decisions integrate quantitative screening with qualitative management assessment and systematic risk evaluation.

Competitive Differentiation: The investment team's established global networks provide institutional-level due diligence capabilities typically unavailable to similarly-sized managers. This infrastructure advantage, combined with sector expertise spanning technology, industrials, chemicals, and telecommunications, enables identification of overlooked opportunities in less-efficient international markets.

results.strategy_description:
The Artisan Partners Credit Team launched the Artisan Credit Opportunities Fund with a straight-forward goal: generating attractive risk-adjusted returns through an opportunistic approach that pursues long and short investments along the capital structure of leveraged corporate issuers. Using a high-conviction, bottom-up fundamental research process, our team looks to take advantage of the illiquidity premium and inherently asymmetric risk profile of credit investments across multiple sectors, regions and styles. Having honed our skills through years of investing in the asset class, we believe the disciplined execution of our process enables the building of a portfolio that can deliver value regardless of the market environment.

The team utilizes quantitative screens and qualitative factors to identify overlooked and under-appreciated investment opportunities. The team’s research process has four primary pillars: business quality, financial strength and flexibility, downside analysis and value identification.
results.region_exposure_description: There are no specific limits on the instrument type or geographic location of the portfolio’s holdings in the Credit Opportunities strategy. Under normal market conditions, the team expects high yield bonds and leveraged loans to make up the majority of the investments. While the strategy is not geographically constrained, the team’s expertise and experience leads them to focus primarily on US-based issuers. Attractive investments are, however, occasionally found outside of the US, most commonly in Canada and Europe.

In August 2018, the partnership assumed advisement of Claren Road Credit Master Fund, Ltd. (CMF) which launched in 2006. With an average of 27 years of extensive experience in global credit markets, the Partners have traded long and short throughout multiple economic and market cycles.

results.portfolio_additional_details: The Strategy seeks to invest globally across sectors, issuers, regions, and maturity curves with a focus on Investment Grade and Large Cap High Yield. It seeks to identify convex single name long and short investments in cash and CDS. Generally, the Fund does not take a large directional bias and seeks to be uncorrelated. It seeks to be long volatility: negative carry is a unique byproduct of the strategy.
results.esg_approach_description: Compass Rose has given consideration to a range of codes and standards, including the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment and the United Nations Global Compact, and developed an ESG policy and guidelines for conduct in these areas.  The Firm understands that ESG issues are evolving and will continue to give it appropriate consideration. The portfolio follows a heavily trading-oriented, dynamic and diversified strategy. This leads to frequent monthly turnover with no observable structural / market directional bias. Due to the active trading nature of the strategy, the Firm has not implemented ESG factors into its investment process and does not make or restrict investments solely on the basis of ESG

The Lynx Program is our original strategy that was launched in May 2000. It is a diversified managed futures program that aims to deliver high risk-adjusted returns with attractive portfolio characteristics. While the primary approach is systematic trend-following applied cross a broad universe of global futures and foreign exchange markets, a portion of the risk is allocated to complementary models that are designed to enhance performance in non-trending market environments. These diversifying models utilize a variety of concepts from quantitative macro to machine learning. The program attempts to identify opportunities across time frames, holding positions from only a few days to over a year.

Lynx UCITS Fund launched 1 March 2019. Prior, the fund ran on the FundLogic Alternatives platform from 6 June 2014 as MS Lynx UCITS Fund. The Lynx UCITS Fund is a subfund to the Lynx UCITS Funds ICAV.

results.name: Lynx 1.5 (Bermuda) Ltd.
results.strategy_description: The Lynx Program is our original strategy that was launched in May 2000. The objective of the Lynx Program is to generate a high risk-adjusted return while maintaining attractive portfolio characteristics. The characteristics have been chosen with the aim of making the strategy suitable as a building block in an institutional investor's portfolio. Examples of these characteristics include a low correlation to equities and bonds, a positive correlation to volatility and positive skewness of returns. Other characteristics relate to the ability to react to trend reversals and profit from prolonged bear market conditions (often referred to as "crisis alpha"). The Lynx Program's main approach is systematic advanced trend following. The program is employing a multi-model approach applying a range of statistical techniques to identify and capture trends over a span of time frames. In addition to trend following concepts, the strategy includes an allocation to diversifying models that aim to exploit other market phenomena than price momentum. These diversifying models consists of systematic global macro concepts based on fundamental data as well as models utilizing various machine learning techniques. In total the program consists of approximately 40 different models. The Investment Committee is responsible for strategy including setting the risk allocation to each model in the program.

results.name: Lynx Systematic Macro Fund (Bermuda) Ltd.
results.strategy_description: The Lynx Systematic Macro Program uses fundamental macroeconomic principles to invest broadly across currencies, fixed income, equity indices and commodities. The program combines around 100 proprietary signals designed to capitalize on unique inefficiencies and market phenomena and are segregated into themes including macro and monetary, valuation dynamics, risk sentiment, market dynamics and term structure dynamics. A completely integrated and systematized investment methodology is employed, from signal generation and portfolio construction to execution and risk management. The program trades across timeframes with positions expected to last from just a few days to multiple months. A portfolio optimization approach is utilized to maximize risk adjusted returns with constraints on thematic and asset class exposures to ensure broad participation in diverse opportunities over time. Additionally, the program attempts to limit directionality to minimize correlations to both traditional and alternative investment strategies. The Lynx Systematic Macro Program targets an annualized volatility of 15% gross of fees.
